(Since ancient times, countless people have for the most part been bound by fate, unable to make their own decisions. Only those of great goodness cannot be bound by fate; this is what is meant by saying that the perfected person holds the key to transforming destiny! [◆ qishu: fortune, fate. zhiren: a person of exceedingly lofty moral cultivation.])

Liaofan's Four Lessons is known throughout the world as a treasure book for transforming destiny. A person of great blessings, once he obtains this book, naturally recites it with whole-hearted reverence, never tiring of reading it a hundred times, and passes from understanding to practice. And so he turns illness into health, poverty into prosperity, transgression into blessing, and the ordinary into the sagely. By it one cultivates oneself, and everyone may become a sage or worthy; by it one cultivates the world, and the whole world may dissolve its disasters and hindrances. This is the gateway of skillful means for saving oneself and saving others!

(Do the young people of today ever fail to be great in aspiration and great in speech, possessing the grand bearing of one who would clarify the universe — yet in the end they accomplish nothing. The reason is simply that their own foundation is not established. Liaofan's Four Lessons is truly the great foundation for establishing oneself, preserving one's work, and governing the world! This book teaches by personal example and shows people real results; if one can read it thoroughly and put it into practice, then destiny is created by me and blessings are made by me, and there is nothing under heaven that cannot be done. A worthy person or gentleman who obtains this single text and reverently stores it in his breast will thereby turn his own intent around and open, on level ground, a road to the clouds. Moreover, to bring blessing to the common people and to turn back the calamities of the final age is the very first undertaking of our participation in the transforming nurture of Heaven and Earth, and the supreme foundation of regulating the family and governing the state. How can one drudge away after fame and gain and willingly degrade and abandon oneself? How much more so when, having urged one person onward and he becomes a sage or worthy, or a Bodhisattva, the good karma he accomplishes throughout his entire life cannot be counted, and the ignorant people he teaches cannot be counted either? All of this comes from the gentleman who awakened him, and so his merit and virtue are equal to that person's. Set beside those who chase fame and gain they can never be sure to win, it is as far apart as heaven and earth!

(Mr. Liaofan kept the Ledger of Merits and Demerits: every thought that arose in his mind, and every word and deed, good or evil, he recorded without the least omission, so that his good thoughts, good words and good deeds might increase day by day while his evil thoughts, evil words and evil deeds decreased day by day. At first good and evil were still mixed together; as he persevered, in time there was only good and no evil. Thus he was able to turn a life without blessing into one with blessing, to turn a short life into a long one, and to turn childlessness into many descendants. While alive he rose to the realm of sages and worthies, and when his reward here was exhausted he was reborn in the highest grade in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. His conduct was a model for the multitude, his words a standard for the world. Since Mr. Liaofan could transform his own destiny and become a great man, so can I. Here, “you have sat for three days and I have seen not one deluded thought arise” means that Master Liaofan sat in quiet meditation for three days and was able to concentrate his mind on one point, free of distracting thoughts. Note: in the practice of Chan concentration there are four stages: the first, second, third and fourth dhyana. Before the first dhyana come the coarse abiding, the subtle abiding, the concentration of the realm of desire, and the concentration not yet reached. In the first dhyana, the breath stops. When the outer breath stops, the inner breath becomes active, as in hibernation. At such a time the mind is clear as water and bright as a mirror. This may last a day, or even a month or a year, without the settled mind decaying. Master Liaofan later wrote a piece entitled Essential Methods of Quiet Sitting. In its preface he says: “My teacher, the Great Master Yungu, sat in quiet meditation for more than twenty years and wondrously attained the legacy of Tiantai, and he spoke to me of it in full detail.” [Tiantai] that is, the Tiantai school. “Tiantai” is the name of a mountain in Tiantai county, Taizhou, in Zhejiang province; in the Sui dynasty the Great Zhiyi lived on this mountain and founded a school, and later ages therefore called his school the Tiantai school, abbreviated to Tiantai or the Tai school. The Great Zhiyi wrote a one-fascicle work, Calm and Insight for Beginners, known to the world as the Lesser Calm and Insight of Tiantai, which is the essential method for cultivating calm and insight in sitting

Note: when one recites a mantra until ten thousand thoughts return to one and no second thought arises, this is called passing the first gate. When one recites until reciting yet not reciting, not reciting yet reciting, this is called samā dhi appearing, also called passing the second gate. [the three gates of mantra recitation] " What is the first gate? When a student recites a true word (mantra) until ten thousand thoughts return to one and no second thought arises, this is called passing the first gate. But this is still pressing down grass with a stone, and is not yet ultimate. What is the second gate? title: Annotated Liaofan's Four Lessons
author: Annotated by Mingde
excerpt: Since ancient times countless people have been bound by fate and could not make their own decisions. Only the greatly good cannot be bound by fate; as it is said, the perfected person has a knack for creating destiny.
